thread:
Maria Chen: Heads-up — sharing a short CS cheat snippet for surge-proofing customer onboardings. Focus: minimize renewal risk during first 14d by managing latency spikes via caching + batching + streaming.

Ben Alvarez: Love it. quick question: do we suggest client-side backoff or server-side queueing first?

Maria Chen: start server-side queueing + prefix cache. client backoff as fallback. keep SLOs: p50 < 100ms for example flows.

Kiana Patel: adding a small sample config we used with Acme that lowered token cost and avoided TTL churn:
```yaml
cache:
  ttl: 20m
  prefill: true
  keys: ['tenant_id', 'flow_sig']
batching:
  max_batch_size: 6
  max_latency_ms: 40
streaming:
  enabled: true
  low_watermark_tokens: 16
```

Rahul Singh: also note: for high churn accounts, set cache.ttl shorter and use ephemeral warm pools; also tag renewal-risk if >500 errors in 24h.

Maria Chen: Suggested CS play: at T+48h, run 'activation health check' and surface renewal_signal metric to AE. Script below:
```bash
# activation health
curl -s -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" "https://api.redwood.ai/v1/customers/$TENANT/health" | jq .
```

Ben Alvarez: can we add a simple feedback capture hook in the streaming response? e.g., stream a short survey after the final token.

Kiana Patel: Yep — example: append a small structured event: {"type":"feedback_prompt","url":"/cs/quick-survey"}

ops-bot: Note: scheduled job 'cs-activation-scan' will run daily at 03:00 UTC and tag tenants with renewal_risk if errors>threshold :white_check_mark:

Maria Chen: action items: 1) add snippet to customer-facing docs 2) CS runbook: T+24/48 checks 3) Enable streaming feedback for pilot accounts (Acme). I'll coordinate with Rahul on warm-pools. @Ben Alvarez @Kiana Patel please ack.

Ben Alvarez: ack :thumbsup:

Kiana Patel: ack :white_check_mark:

Rahul Singh: ack, will spin up a warm-pool template.

Maria Chen: thanks — saving to /cs/cs-ops/snippets/surge-proofing-quick.json and will put on the enablement deck.
